jobs.title: Full-Stack Engineer (Backend Leaning) - Studio
jobs.description:
ABOUT ELEVENLABS

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

 - ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

 - ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

 - ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.




HOW WE WORK

 - High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

 - Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

 - AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

 - Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

 - Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.




WHAT WE OFFER

 - Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

 - Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

 - Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

 - Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

 - Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún

 - Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role
Studio is where creators build and finish video on ElevenLabs, powered by our generative graph engine, Flows. You’ll own our “produce once, distribute everywhere” workflow. It takes a finished Studio project and runs it through our dubbing pipeline to produce it in many languages and aspect ratios, with auto-translated captions. Today that means duplicating and rebuilding projects by hand.
This work is entirely greenfield: the specs aren’t written yet. You’ll shape them through written proposals (RFCs), pressure-test data structures with the team lead, and carry the project from first draft to launch.
You’re a strong backend generalist who is good with complex data structures and has the product instincts to decide what’s worth building.


Requirements

 - Strong backend generalist who has designed and shipped complex, data-heavy systems end to end.

 - Comfortable with enterprise-grade concerns such as usage reporting and accounts.

 - Evidence of product ownership: side projects, open source, or work in a product-facing context.

 - Has taken projects from inception to launch with little hand-holding.

Bonus: experience with media or video-processing pipelines (helpful, not required)

We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender

jobs.title: IT Systems Engineer
jobs.description:
The Role: 

Scale AI is hiring a highly skilled foundational IT Systems Engineer for our Public Sector IT team to design, build, and operate secure, scalable infrastructure that empowers employees to do their best work. You’ll join a creative, fast-moving, solutions-oriented group that architects and implements automation across identity and access management, endpoint management, and our broader SaaS stack. Leveraging Okta, Gsuite, AWS, and your familiarity with federal frameworks (FedRAMP High, IL6, CMMC), you’ll deliver robust, audit-ready systems that meet stringent compliance requirements. The ideal candidate pairs deep IAM best practices and hands-on SaaS administration with a zero-trust mindset, clear documentation, and a genuine drive to make people happy, while protecting system integrity in a fast-paced, high-security environment.

You will:

  • Assist with the administration of our tech stack with platforms such as Okta, Opal, Slack, Jamf, Jira, and many more
  • Provide escalated assistance to the IT Services and Support team
  • Partner with Security/Compliance on audit artifacts (SSP updates, POA&Ms, control mappings to NIST 800-53/171, CMMC 2.0).
  • Create and update technology documentation for internal IT teams and Scale employees
  • Design and maintain Zero-Trust controls (device posture, network segmentation, Conditional Access) across Okta.
  • Build automation workflows and lightweight services (webhooks/queues) to automate joiner–mover–leaver events, access reviews, and deprovisioning.
  • Own change management for IT systems in regulated environments (CAB records, rollback plans, validation evidence).

Ideally you'd have:

  • 5+ years of IT systems, infrastructure, and/or engineering experience
  • Experience with integrating with SaaS APIs and SDKs
  • Experience with leveraging Okta or similar identity management systems for authentication and provisioning methods such as SAML, OIDC, and SCIM
  • Scripting experience with Python, Powershell, and/or bash
  • Experience working within SCIFs 
  • Familiarity with IL6 / FedRAMP High / CMMC 2.0 control families and how they translate to concrete IT configs

Nice to haves:

  • IT Security and Compliance focused mindset
  • Familiarity with Infrastructure-as-Code for identity/MDM configs (e.g., Terraform providers for Okta/Jamf/Azure)
  • Possession of an active Secret or TS/SCI clearance

Compensation packages at Scale for eligible roles include base salary, equity, and benefits. The range displayed on each job posting reflects the minimum and maximum target for new hire salaries for the position and may be inclusive of several career levels at Scale; it will be determined during the interview process based on work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, qualifications, interview performance, and relevant education or training. Scale employees in eligible roles are also granted equity based compensation, subject to Board of Director approval. Your recruiter can share more about the specific salary range for your preferred location during the hiring process, and confirm whether the hired role will be eligible for equity grant. You'll also receive benefits including, but not limited to: comprehensive health, dental and vision coverage, retirement benefits, a learning and development stipend, and generous PTO. Additionally, this role may be eligible for additional benefits such as a commuter stipend.

The base salary range for this full-time position in the location of Washington DC is:
$148,800—

jobs.title: Jr. Software Engineer - Full Time - (Strictly OPT Candidates Only)
jobs.description:
Junior Software Engineer – Full-Time

All ove USA (Washington, California, Texas, Virginia, Georgia, Calorado, Massachusetts and many more)

Salary: $75,000 – $80,000 / year

Visa Sponsorship: OPT (F-1) eligible candidates welcome

About The Role

We are looking for a motivated Junior Software Engineer to join one of our engineering teams in Washington. This is a full-time opportunity ideal for recent graduates or early-career engineers who are eager to build real-world, high-scale systems. You will work with experienced engineers, contribute to production code, and grow your skills in a fast-paced, customer-obsessed environment.

What You’ll Do

• Design, develop, test, and maintain software features using Java and/or Python
• Write clean, efficient, and well-documented code that follows engineering best practices
• Collaborate with senior engineers, product managers, and cross-functional teams to deliver features end-to-end
• Participate in code reviews, debugging, and performance optimization
• Learn and apply leadership principles and operational excellence practices
• Contribute to continuous improvement of systems, tools, and processes

Basic Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field (or equivalent practical experience)
• 0–2 years of professional software development experience (internships, co-ops, or strong academic projects count)
• Proficiency in Java and/or Python
• Solid understanding of data structures, algorithms, and object-oriented programming
• Familiarity with version control (Git), basic Linux/Unix commands, and software development lifecycle
• Strong problem-solving skills and willingness to learn
• OPT (F-1) visa status or eligibility preferred; we support OPT candidates

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience with at least one of: REST APIs, microservices, SQL/NoSQL databases, or cloud services (AWS preferred)
• Academic or personal projects demonstrating clean coding practices and system design basics
• Familiarity with Agile/Scrum methodologies
• Excellent communication skills and ability to work in a collaborative team environment

What We Offer

• Competitive base salary of $75,000 – $80,000 per year
• Full-time employment with comprehensive benefits (medical, dental, vision, 401(k), employee discounts, and more)
• Opportunity to work on systems that impact millions of customers
• Career growth paths within the engineering organization

Location

This role is based in Washington state. Hybrid expectations will be confirmed during the interview process.

How to Apply

If you are an early-career engineer passionate about building reliable software at scale and currently on (or eligible for) OPT, we encourage you to apply. Please submit your resume highlighting relevant projects, coursework, and any internship experience.

jobs.title: Delivery Solutions Architect - Startups & Emerging Enterprise
jobs.location: Remote - California; Remote - Colorado; Remote - Illinois; Remote - Massachusetts; Remote - New York; Remote - Oregon; Remote - Texas; Remote - Washington
jobs.description:
At Databricks, we are on a mission to empower our customers to solve the world's toughest data problems by utilizing the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform. As a Delivery Solutions Architect (DSA), you will play an important role during this journey. You will collaborate with our sales and field engineering teams to accelerate the adoption and growth of the Databricks platform with Startup and Emerging Enterprise customers. You will also help ensure customer success by helping our most complex customers maximize the value they get out of our platform and their return on investment.

This is a hybrid technical and commercial role. It is commercial in the sense that you will drive growth in your assigned customers and use cases by leading your customers' stakeholders, building executive relationships, orchestrating other focused/specialized teams within Databricks, and creating and driving plans and strategies for Databricks colleagues to build upon. It is technical in the sense that you will serve as the post-sale technical lead across all Databricks products. This requires you to use your skills and technical credibility to engage and communicate at all levels within an organization. You will report directly to a DSA Manager within the Field Engineering organization. 

The impact you will have:

  • Engage with Solutions Architects to understand the full use case demand plan for prioritized customers
  • Lead the post-technical-win account strategy and execution plan for the majority of Databricks use cases within our most strategic accounts
  • Be the accountable technical leader for specific use cases and customers across multiple selling teams and internal stakeholders, creating certainty from uncertainty and driving onboarding, enablement, go-live, and healthy consumption of the workloads the customer has chosen to run on Databricks
  • Be the first contact for any technical issues or questions related to production/go live status of agreed upon use cases within an account, often spanning multiple use cases within the largest and most complex organizations
  • Leverage Shared Services, User Education, Onboarding/Technical Services, and Support resources, and escalate to subject matter experts when work falls beyond your scope or expertise
  • Create, own, and execute a point of view on how key use cases can be accelerated into production, coordinating with Professional Services (PS) resources on the delivery of PS Engagement proposals
  • Partner with Databricks Product and Engineering teams on new product innovations, private previews, and upgrades
  • Develop an execution plan spanning all customer-facing technical roles and teams across the following work streams:
    • Main use cases moving from ‘win’ to production
    • Enablement / user growth plan
    • Product adoption (strategy and activities to increase adoption of Databricks’ Lakehouse vision)
    • Organic needs for current investment (e.g. cloud cost control, tuning & optimization)
    • Executive and operational governance
  • Provide internal and external updates to your Technical GM — KPI reporting on usage and customer health, covering investment status, key risks, product adoption, and use case progression

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

jobs.description:
ABOUT ELEVENLABS

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

 - ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

 - ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

 - ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.




HOW WE WORK

 - High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

 - Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

 - AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

 - Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

 - Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.




WHAT WE OFFER

 - Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

 - Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

 - Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

 - Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

 - Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún

 - Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.


THE ROLE

ElevenLabs runs a deliberately lean finance team across 10+ legal entities and 40+ countries. The stack is built around NetSuite, Stripe, Ramp, Deel, HiBob and Pigment, with a BigQuery/dbt warehouse underneath. We want a close where people review exceptions and agents handle the rest. You'll own that stack, from architecture and integrations to controls and vendors. This is a builder role, not a ticket queue.

 - Run NetSuite end to end. That covers multi-subsidiary setup, chart of accounts and segments, scripting and workflows, release management, and roles and segregation of duties as we build toward public-company controls.

 - Own the integration layer: Stripe, Ramp, Deel and HiBob into NetSuite, and NetSuite into the warehouse. Month-end should reconcile by design instead of by hand.

 - Lead selection and rollout of new systems, including usage-based billing and equity administration. You'll also handle the finance setup of every new entity.

 - Build with AI, alongside our Automations and Data teams. Examples include agents and automations for invoice coding, people-cost reconciliations and accounting requests.

 - Be the systems voice in finance decisions on new pricing models, new geographies and audit readiness.




REQUIREMENTS

 - You've administered a multi-entity NetSuite OneWorld instance y

jobs.title: AI Systems Engineer - DevOps& Observability Manager
jobs.description:
Location: Anywhere in Country

At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.

We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go. Join EY and help to build a better working world.

The opportunity

We are seeking an AI Systems Engineer to own the delivery, model-serving, routing, and observability layer of EY’s AI-native platform. These are the systems that ship, run, and make fully visible every AI workload. Within the Hybrid AI Multi-Environment Runtime (HAI), this role owns how AI services and agents are built and deployed, how models execute, how requests are routed to them, how AI assets are catalogued and governed, how consumption is measured and bounded, and how the entire platform is observed across cloud, on-prem, edge, and air-gapped environments.

This is a distinct discipline from platform, data, and trust engineering. Where Platform Engineering owns the cluster substrate and its infrastructure automation, this role owns the delivery and runtime surface, including the CI/CD/CV pipelines that ship AI workloads, secure model execution, semantic routing, and model/prompt selection, together with the governance, discovery, cost, and telemetry systems that keep AI workloads shippable, economical, discoverable, and transparent. It sits at the intersection of DevOps, MLOps, FinOps, and observability.

This role is ideal for an engineer who is equally comfortable building automated delivery pipelines, operating high-performance inference (GPUs, model servers, sandboxed execution), and building deep observability and cost visibility; who understands that in regulated contexts every AI workload must be delivered repeatably and every AI request must be economically bounded, attributable, and traceable end-to-end.

Your Key Responsibilities

• Own DevOps and delivery for AI workloads: build and operate the CI/CD/CV pipelines that ship AI services, agents, and runtime components, including automated build, test, continuous verification, release, and rollback, so AI workloads are delivered repeatably and safely into every environment.
• Own governance and discovery for AI assets, including service catalog/registry (Artifactory/Nexus, Harbor), experiment tracking and model metadata (MLflow), upstream registries/mirrors (HuggingFace/NGC), CVE/SBOM scanning (Trivy), lineage contracts (OpenLineage), and license management.
• Own resource and cost management, including quotas and rate limits, cost attribution and utilization (Apptio/OpenCost/Kubecost), so AI execution stays economically bounded and controllable per tenant and engagement.
• Own the full observability stack, including metrics (Prometheus/Mimir), logs (Loki), traces (Tempo/Jaeger), dashboards (Grafana), LLM debugging and evaluation (LangSmith/Langfuse), and SLA/alert notifications.
• Own the OpenTelemetry collection layer, including multi-tenant receiver, exporters and queues (Kafka sink), DCGM exporter for GPU telemetry, processor batching, and dynamic filtering, so every signal is captured and routed reliably.
• Automate GitOps-based delivery and continuous verification; embedding quality, integrity, and cost gates into pipelines so releases are policy-compliant by default rather than by manual review.
• Close the loop between delivery and observability by using telemetry, evaluation, and cost signals to drive deployment decisions, progressive rollout, and automated rollback of AI workloads.
• Ensure cost and telemetry are identity-stamped and per-tenant, so consumption and behavior are attributable end-to-end, keeping FinOps and observability tied to the workloads that generate the load.

Skills And Attributes For Success

• Strong DevOps expertise: CI/CD/CV pipeline design, GitOps, continuous verification, and progressive/automated release and rollback for production workloads.
• Deep expertise operating model-serving and inference systems (Ray, vLLM/Triton/NIM) on GPUs at production

PERPLEXITY API PLATFORM

Perplexity innovates at the frontier of AI infrastructure, search, and orchestration to serve the world's most discerning users. The Perplexity API Platform brings our technology to the world's most discerning developers. From exabyte-scale knowledge indexes to codegen-first agent runtimes, the building blocks behind Perplexity's applications are some of the most battle-tested AI systems in the industry.

We believe these same building blocks can and should power the aspirations of builders everywhere. It's one thing to solve planet-scale retrieval, long-horizon orchestration, and other foundational AI challenges within a single product ecosystem. The true measure of success is to turn those solutions into elegant APIs that delight developers and agents alike. Our API Platform delivers frontier intelligence to thousands of customers: startups, trillion-dollar enterprises, U.S. and allied governments, and everyone in between.

We've achieved incredible scale, yet we're just getting started. Join us to build tools for curious minds.




ABOUT THIS ROLE

Perplexity is seeking strong engineers with a passion for delivering frontier intelligence and infrastructure to developers. Our company builds technology that reshapes how people search, reason, and interact with the world around them. Week after week, we observe increasing demand for programmatic interfaces to that technology. The API Platform engineering team is charged with designing, implementing, and scaling these interfaces.

As a member of our team, you'll work on an eclectic portfolio spanning distributed systems, performance optimization, agent orchestration, and frontier topics that often change with each passing month. Throughout this work, you'll prioritize great developer and agent experience alike. You'll also define technical strategy for how we scale to meet compounding growth exponentials (number of customers, agents per customer, compute/retrieval per agent, etc.).




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Design, build, and operate mission-critical APIs that provide our customers the building blocks for frontier intelligence.

 - Own and evolve the API gateway and routing layer: authentication, authorization, rate limiting and quotas, usage metering, and request routing across heterogeneous upstream services.

 - Build the paved road for API services: standardized service scaffolding, container builds, CI/CD, Kubernetes and Helm deployment, and progressive rollouts with fast rollback, so a new API product goes from idea to production in days, not weeks.

 - Build API governance into the platform: contract-first schemas, breaking-change detection in CI, versioning and deprecation workflows, and SDKs and documentation generated from a single source of truth.

 - Unify cross-cutting capabilities (billing and usage, rate limiting, organization and identity settings, analytics and observability) so every API product gets them by default instead of rebuilding them.

jobs.description:
At Snowflake, we are powering the era of the agentic enterprise. To usher in this new era, we seek AI-native thinkers across every function who are energized by the opportunity to reinvent how they work. You don’t just use tools; you possess an innate curiosity, treating AI as a high-trust collaborator that is core to how you solve problems and accelerate your impact. We look for low-ego individuals who thrive in dynamic and fast-moving environments and move with an experimental mindset — who rapidly test emerging capabilities to discover simpler, more powerful ways to deliver results. At Snowflake, your role isn't just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done.
Senior Software Engineer — Cortex Training
The Snowflake ML Platform team's mission is to let customers run their most demanding ML/AI workloads inside Snowflake. Cortex Training is our LLM post-training platform: it turns scarce, expensive GPU capacity into a simple, composable service, so customers can adapt open-weight foundation models to their own business problems while we handle the hard distributed-systems parts, including scheduling, orchestration, multi-node training and inference, fault tolerance, and throughput.
The platform already runs post-training at scale. Under the hood, it decouples GPU computation from the training loop and exposes it as primitive APIs that compose into everything from SFT to full RL workflows. You'll work alongside a team that ships fast & sweats reliability and the researchers behind DeepSpeed. We're looking for an engineer who thrives in the ML infrastructure layer and brings a solid understanding of LLMs and post-training to help us scale and grow it.

YOU WILL:
• Design and build across the full stack — from the public training APIs and SDK through the control plane to the GPU data plane.

• Scale the distributed systems that make GPU compute serverless — multi-tenant scheduling, placement, and capacity-aware routing across regional GPU pools, with fault tolerance built in.

• Drive end-to-end performance at scale — keep the training, inference, and RL loops fast and the data plane responsive under heavy concurrent load, with GPUs kept saturated.

• Productionize research building blocks — partner with Snowflake Research to turn state-of-the-art training and inference techniques into reliable, composable components customers can run at enterprise scale.

QUALIFICATIONS:
• 3 + years (Intermediate) | 6+ years (Senior) building and shipping production ML systems

• Strong distributed systems and infrastructure foundation — designing scalable, fault-tolerant services and operating them on Kubernetes in production.

• Familiarity with GPU and LLM infrastructure — e.g., PyTorch, DeepSpeed/FSDP, Ray, CUDA/NCCL, vLLM; able to debug across the data, infrastructure, and GPU layers.

• Demonstrated ability to harden complex systems for reliability, throughput, and cost efficiency.

• BS in Computer Science or a related field (MS/PhD a plus).

• (Bonus) Hands-on LLM post-training / modeling experience — the strongest candidates pair deep infra skills with real post-training intuition.

Snowflake is growing fast, and we’re scaling our team to help enable and accelerate our growth. We are looking for people who share our values, challenge ordinary thinking, and push the pace of innovation while building a future for themselves and Snowflake.

jobs.title: Data Engineer
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY; Seattle, WA
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic's go-to-market teams are scaling quickly, and the decisions they make, from who to sell to and how to cover them to where to invest next, are only as good as the intelligence and infrastructure underneath them. As a Data Engineer on the GTM Systems data foundations team, you'll help build that layer: the data products that give sellers, operators, and analysts a rich, current, and trusted picture of the market, and the engineering rigor that lets our GTM systems run reliably as the business grows.

This is an engineering role that goes beyond pipelines. You'll treat GTM data as a product and a platform: built once, kept current, and available wherever people work. Alongside the build, you'll help shape what the data means: how attributes are defined, which sources are trusted, and how the business puts them to use. The role sits at the intersection of the sales organization, the data organization, and the systems that data flows through. You'll partner closely with Sales Strategy and Operations, Finance, Data Science, and the central data engineering team.

Key responsibilities

  • Bring disparate internal and external sources together: orchestrate, model, and normalize first-party product and revenue data alongside third-party data into one usable understanding of the company landscape

  • Build and maintain identity and entity resolution, so every source attaches to one trusted record for each company and the relationships between companies are clear

  • Help build the canonical layer where key attributes are defined once and mean the same thing everywhere, with clear sourcing logic, provenance, and freshness

  • Turn data into intelligence: scores, signals, and AI-generated attributes that help GTM teams prioritize and act, held to the same quality bar as any other source

  • Deliver that intelligence to the surfaces where teams work, including the CRM, and bring production discipline to how data moves through those systems

  • Operate what you build as a living system, with observability, data quality, cost, security, and access controls designed in, so problems surface before the field sees them

  • Partner with the owners of GTM processes such as planning, segmentation, and routing to settle definitions, make clear commitments, and communicate tradeoffs

  • Make the platform easy for other teams to build on, so work is contributed once and not rebuilt in silos

Minimum qualifications

  • Experience as a data engineer or analytics engineer building and operating production pipelines and data models

  • Strong SQL and Python, and experience with modern transformation and orchestration tooling on a cloud data warehouse

  • Experience making messy data from many sources usable, including record matching, deduplication, and reconciling conflicting values

  • Familiarity with go-to-market data and the CRM systems it flows through

  • Judgment beyond the pipeline: weighing data sources, shaping definitions with business partners, and making calls on data quality

  • Clear written and verbal communication with technical and non-technical partners

  • Regular hands-on use of AI tools in your engineering work

Preferred qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience in data engineering, analytics engineering, or GTM data roles

jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Training and serving frontier AI models requires compute infrastructure at a scale and density that pushes past what conventional data center designs were built to handle. Anthropic's Data Center Infrastructure team is responsible for delivering that physical infrastructure — partnering with build partners, equipment manufacturers, and utilities to stand up facilities that can reliably power some of the largest accelerator clusters in the industry. At the scale we build, our campuses are typically served by dedicated high-voltage substations and a medium-voltage distribution network that may also integrate on-site generation and battery energy storage — and the protection, control, and automation layer is what keeps all of it selective, coordinated, and observable.

 

As a Data Center Substation, Protection & Automation Engineer, you'll own the protection and automation architecture across Anthropic's US portfolio — from the utility point of interconnection (POI) through the HV/MV substation, the MV distribution loop, and down into LV switchgear. You'll develop and maintain our protection philosophy and reference relay settings, run and review the short-circuit, coordination, and arc-flash studies that underpin them, design the substation automation and SCADA architecture, and define how relays and meters integrate into the electrical power monitoring system (EPMS) — giving operators real-time visibility and sequence-of-events data when something trips. You'll also be our technical lead on the protection side of utility interconnection — working relay settings, transfer-trip, and ride-through requirements with transmission owners and ISOs/RTOs.

 

Protection engineering and substation automation are the core of this role; substation physical design is a strong plus but not a prerequisite — we'd like to hear from protection and P&C engineers who have spent their careers on relays, schemes, and studies even if they haven't owned a substation general arrangement. You'll work closely with colleagues across the infrastructure team, our build partners' A/E firms, relay and switchgear vendors, and utility protection groups. Expect roughly 20–35% travel for witnessing factory acceptance and relay testing, and supporting site energization and commissioning.

Responsibilities

Protection engineering

  • Own Anthropic's protection philosophy and basis of design across the electrical system — HV substation, MV distribution, generator and energy-storage interties, and LV switchgear — and maintain the reference relay settings and protection one-line templates our build partners design against

  • Specify protective relays and develop relay settings for transformer, feeder, bus, generator, motor, and arc-flash protection applications, working across major platforms (e.g., SEL, GE Multilin, ABB, Siemens, Schneider)

  • Perform and critically review short-circuit, protective-device coordination, and arc-flash studies; use findings to steer equipment selection, settings, and incident-energy mitigation

  • Implement automatic transfer, load-shed, and restoration schemes in protection and automation logic, and make sure they stay secure and coordinated under every credible contingency

  • Review protection and control design packages, relay settings calculations, and coordination studies from build partners and A/E firms against our basis of design, and drive closure on deviations and exceptions

jobs.title: Data Center Power Generation and Microgrids Engineer
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Training and serving frontier AI models requires compute infrastructure at a scale and density that pushes past what conventional data center designs were built to handle. The loads involved are large enough — and arrive fast enough — that utility supply alone often can't meet the need on the timeline required, and the step-load behavior of large accelerator clusters creates power-quality and ride-through demands that conventional backup-generation designs weren't built for. Anthropic's Data Center Infrastructure team is responsible for solving that problem: delivering facilities that can be energized early, ride through grid disturbances, and present a well-behaved load at the point of interconnection (POI).

 

As a Data Center Power Generation & Microgrids Engineer, you'll own the behind-the-meter generation and storage architecture for Anthropic's data center portfolio. That means the on-site generation fleet — reciprocating engine gensets, gas turbines, fuel cells — and the battery energy storage systems that buffer load steps and provide ride-through. It means the microgrid layer that ties them together: islanding and resynchronization, black-start, load-shedding, and generation dispatch. And it means the grid side: interconnection studies and agreements, IEEE 1547/2800 compliance, and power quality at the point of interconnection. You'll also own our temporary- and bridging-generation strategies — the plans that let a site energize and start serving load before permanent utility service is available, and transition cleanly once it is.

This is a deeply cross-functional role. You'll work closely with colleagues across the infrastructure team on where and how generation and storage tie into the site electrical distribution, controls, and SCADA, and with our hardware and compute teams to understand the load characteristics you're designing against. You'll be Anthropic's technical counterpart to on-site generation providers, BESS integrators, utilities, and ISOs/RTOs. Expect roughly 20–35% travel for design reviews, factory witness testing, and site startup.

Responsibilities

On-site generation engineering

  • Own Anthropic's behind-the-meter generation architecture across the portfolio — prime-mover selection and sizing (reciprocating engines, gas turbines, fuel cells), paralleling topology, redundancy, fuel systems, and emissions controls — and maintain the generation basis of design and technical specifications that build partners and generation providers design against

  • Set the day-one vs. day-N plant sizing and expansion strategy — what the plant needs on day one so it can be expanded or augmented later, and how to add units, storage, or a grid tie to a system already running

  • Characterize the data center load for external generation partners — step changes, ramps, oscillation, fault behavior, and non-IT load — so providers can size and tune their plant against the real duty

  • Model generation response against the load profile of large-scale ML training — step-load acceptance, block loading, transient frequency and voltage response, load rejection — and set the acceptance criteria (e.g., per ISO 8528-5) that generation packages are tested against

  • Develop temporary- and bridging-generation strategies that deliver early site energization ahead of permanent utility service, including the sequencing, protection, and controls changes needed to transition from temporary to permane

The world's biggest companies come to dataiku.com to figure out how to make AI work for them. Your job is to make that experience fast, sharp, and built to convert. You’ll own the code behind dataiku.com: every component, A/B test, and tracking tag that ships goes through you.

Build

  • Work with marketers and the growth team to embed them into agentic processes.

You are a good fit if:

  • You've spent at least 4+ years in web development, ideally on marketing sites, at an agency, or on a growth team.

  • You're strong in React, JavaScript/TypeScr

Eurofins Scientific is an international life sciences company, providing a unique range of analytical testing services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work with the biggest companies in the world to ensure the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic and labelling is accurate.

The Eurofins network of companies is the global leader in food, environment, pharmaceutical and cosmetic product testing and in agroscience Contract Research Organisation services. It is one of the market leaders in certain testing and laboratory services for genomics, discovery pharmacology, forensics, advanced material sciences and in the support of clinical studies, as well as having an emerging global presence in Contract Development and Manufacturing Organisations. It also has a rapidly developing presence in highly specialised and molecular clinical diagnostic testing and in-vitro diagnostic products.

In over 30 years, Eurofins has grown from one laboratory in Nantes, France to 58,000 staff across a decentralised and entrepreneurial network of 900 laboratories in over 54 countries. Eurofins companies offer a portfolio of over 200,000 analytical methods to evaluate the safety, identity, composition, authenticity, origin, traceability and purity of biological substances and products.

In 2021, Eurofins generated total revenues of EUR 6.72 billion, and has been among the best performing stocks in Europe over the past 20 years.

jobs.description:
Machine Learning Operations (MLOps) Engineer
Position Summary

The MLOps Engineer builds and operates the platform and pipelines that take machine learning and AI models from development into reliable production use. This role owns model deployment, automation, monitoring, and lifecycle management, and serves as the ongoing owner of the enterprise sales forecasting models. Beyond operating the platform, the MLOps Engineer is expected to work inside the models themselves, diagnosing accuracy degradation and applying data science judgment to retune features, algorithms, and model logic so that forecast performance continues to deliver measurable business value. The MLOps Engineer partners closely with Data Science, Data Engineering, and Security teams to bridge experimentation and production, and is accountable for the operational health of models once they are live.
Key Responsibilities

· Design, build, and maintain CI/CD pipelines for model training, validation, deployment, and rollback.

· Productionize models developed by data scientists and vendor partners, converting experimental code into scalable, maintainable, and reproducible pipelines.

· Own ongoing maintenance and performance of the enterprise sales forecasting models, including accuracy tracking, periodic recalibration, and continuous improvement.

· Diagnose forecast accuracy degradation and apply data science techniques to improve results, including feature engineering, algorithm selection, hyperparameter tuning, and adjustment of model logic.

· Evaluate forecast performance using appropriate accuracy measures such as WMAPE, and report results and improvement trends to business stakeholders.

· Translate business context, including promotions, seasonality, café openings and closures, and operational disruptions, into model features and adjustments so forecasts remain useful for planning.

· Partner with Finance, Operations, and Supply Chain to understand how forecasts are consumed and ensure model changes deliver measurable business benefit.

· Deploy and manage models on Vertex AI, including training jobs, endpoints, batch prediction, and pipeline orchestration.

· Operationalize LLM and generative AI workloads, including in-warehouse model invocation from BigQuery, prompt and model version management, and output validation.

· Implement model monitoring for accuracy, drift, data quality, latency, and failure, with automated alerting rather than manual review.

· Build automated retraining workflows with clear promotion criteria and approval gates before a new model version reaches production.

· Establish model registry, versioning, and lineage practices so that every production prediction can be traced to a model version, code commit, and training dataset.

· Manage feature pipelines and ensure consistency between training and serving data to prevent training-serving skew.

· Monitor and optimize compute and inference cost, including model selection, batch versus real-time tradeoffs, and capacity utilization.

· Define and enforce infrastructure-as-code standards for ML environments, including environment promotion from development through production.

· Partner with Security and Privacy teams to ensure models and training data meet data classification, access control, and retention requirements.

· Support model governance and audit requirements by documenting model behavior, validation results, and approval history.

· Troubleshoot production model and pipeline failures, drive root cause analysis, and implement preventive controls.

· Collaborate with Data Engineering to define upstream data requirements and ensure pipeline reliability for model inputs.

· Contribute to architecture reviews and present ML platform designs and operational readiness for approval.

· Mentor engineers and data scientists on production standards, deployment practices, and operational discipline.

Education

· Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Dat

jobs.description:
About Snorkel

Snorkel AI is the frontier AI data lab, helping teams build the data and environments behind high-performing frontier and agentic AI. We combine technology with research-driven AI data development to create datasets, benchmarks, evals, and custom solutions for real-world AI systems. Founded out of the Stanford AI Lab in 2019, Snorkel works with leading AI labs and enterprises to move from better data to better outcomes. 

Excited to help us redefine how AI is built? Apply to be the newest Snorkeler!

In September 2026 we raised a $350 million Series E at a $3.5 billion valuation, and we are scaling our engineering and research teams to meet demand.

The role

Frontier AI data is expensive to make and hard to measure. Every task we deliver is tested against the strongest models, often through many long-running agent rollouts. Your job is to make that process faster, cheaper, and more rigorous with ML and AI

You will be one of the early members of ML & Research Engineering at Snorkel. You will study how frontier-grade data is generated and evaluated, form hypotheses, validate them against real production data, and ship the winners at scale. You will shape the discipline's direction, its standards, and the team that grows around it.

What you'll work on

  • Efficient agentic evals. Cut the cost of long-horizon agent evaluation with adaptive sampling, statistically grounded early stopping, model cascades, caching, and cheap-first gating.
  • AI model routing. Route every eval and judge call to the cheapest model that clears the quality bar, with fallback, monitoring, and cost attribution.
  • Fine-tuned small models. Fine-tune and serve open-weight models (LoRA and other parameter-efficient methods) where they match frontier quality, and know when they don't.
  • Predictive difficulty. Build models that estimate how hard a task is for frontier systems before running a single rollout.
  • Measurement for AI data. Build golden datasets, quantify the accuracy and calibration of LLM-as-judge systems, and make quality reproducible across projects.
  • Research to production. Turn research prototypes into reusable, configurable components that forward deployed engineers and researchers use on every project.

What you'll bring

  • 5+ years building production ML or software systems, with end-to-end ownership from prototype to production
  • Hands-on experience running LLM or ML workloads in production, and comfort reasoning about non-deterministic systems
  • Deep grounding in statistics and experimentation: experiment design, hypothesis testing, sampling, and confidence intervals
  • Strong Python and software engineering fundamentals, including testing, code review, and system design
  • Experience designing evaluations and interpreting results rigorously

About the Role

In this role, you will lead and scale Snorkel’s entire Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) organization. These are the engineers who design, build, and run the data pipelines used by the world’s leading AI labs and enterprises. You’ll shape the function’s direction, drive its execution, and manage our fastest-growing team as it scales from 40 to 100+ engineers.

You’ll set the technical and organizational strategy that turns one-off implementations into reusable solutions—pipelines, evals, augmentations, and environments—and invest in shared ways of working. In our product lifecycle, FDE sits between Research, which defines novel approaches and training needs, and Engineering, which scales our platform and pipelines from 1 to 100. FDE owns the most important middle stretch, taking every new investment from 0 to 1.

Your organization is responsible for both what we deliver and how we deliver it. Just as Engineering is the final gate for what goes to production, FDE is the final gate for every dataset that ships to a customer. Nothing goes out without your team’s sign-off. You’ll also own the pipelines that produce that data, from cost and throughput to latency and efficiency.

This role is for a deeply technical leader who is, first and foremost, a doer. You’ll understand pipeline architecture well enough to challenge designs and propose direction, while coaching your managers and tech leads to think beyond their individual projects. In a fast-moving market where resourcing shifts often, you’ll be the steady hand who keeps teams focused on what customers actually need, not just what was specified.

Main Responsibilities

  • Lead and scale the FDE organization: set the vision, define the operating model and org design, and align team plans and strategy with company priorities.
  • Drive hiring in hypergrowth: build a strong bench of engineering managers and tech leads, and keep the hiring bar high while the organization scales rapidly. You’ll grow to 100+ engineers in the coming quarters.
  • Coach and develop EMs and TLMs who run pods of FDEs, helping them grow from single-project owners into leaders who see and solve problems across the delivery organization.
  • Drive reuse across the organization: identify patterns across bespoke deliveries, have FDE build the first version, and partner with Platform Engineering to scale them company-wide.

jobs.title: Principal Place and Route (PnR) Engineer
jobs.location: Austin, Texas, United States; San Jose, California, United States
jobs.description:
SambaNova is a leader in next-generation AI infrastructure, delivering a full-stack inference platform for customers worldwide. At the core of SambaNova's technology is the RDU (Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit) — a chip built on a dataflow architecture rather than the traditional GPU model. Its decode performance is especially strong for agentic workloads like multi-turn agents, code generation, and long-running applications. RDUs are packaged into SambaRack, rack-scale hardware that lets customers deploy state-of-the-art models with better performance, greater energy efficiency, and faster time to value.

About the team

The Place and Route team writes the software that maps dataflow graphs onto SambaNova’s Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit (RDU). Our tools partition each graph, place the pieces on the chip’s compute and memory units, and route the communication between them. The quality of that mapping sets the throughput of the compiled program, including large language model inference and training. We are looking to grow our team with highly motivated engineers who want to utilize advanced algorithms to solve challenging problems. 

About the Role

You will develop and tune the partitioning, placement, and routing algorithms that map customer workloads onto the RDU. You will work with the compiler team, hardware architects, and performance engineers to model new hardware constraints and trace throughput gaps back to mapping decisions. Your changes will ship in production releases and show up in measured performance.

Responsibilities

  • Develop partitioning, placement, and routing algorithms that meet hardware resource constraints and keep compile times practical
  • Tune PnR results for target workloads, including LLM inference at different batch sizes and concurrency levels
  • Model new hardware constraints and architecture features in our solvers and heuristics as the chip evolves
  • Analyze compiled output with performance engineers and trace throughput gaps back to mapping decisions
  • Build the infrastructure for prototyping, regression testing, and deployment of PnR changes
  • Work with the compiler and hardware teams to define interfaces and resource models

Required Qualifications

  • M.S. or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or related field
  • 3+ years of experience developing optimization or graph algorithms in industry or research
  • Expert knowledge of graph algorithms, partitioning algorithms, combinatorial optimization, or MILP solvers
  • Strong proficiency in C/C++
  • Familiarity with Python
  • Experience designing large, highly parallel, performance-sensitive systems
  • Ability to learn hardware architecture and apply it to improve performance
  • Experience solving NP-hard problems in practice with heuristics, approximation, or pruned exact methods

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with place and route for FPGAs, CGRAs, or other spatial architectures
  • Experience with ML compilers such as MLIR, LLVM, TVM, or XLA
  • Experience with simulated annealing, constraint programming, or SAT/SMT solvers
  • Familiarity with LLM inference stacks such as vLLM and PyTorch
  • Publications at venues such as FPGA, DAC, ICCAD, or MLSys

 

Base Salary Range:

Base Pay Range
$1—$999,999 USD

jobs.title: Full-Stack Engineer - ElevenCreative Enterprise
jobs.description:
ABOUT ELEVENLABS

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

 - ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

 - ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

 - ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.




HOW WE WORK

 - High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

 - Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

 - AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

 - Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

 - Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.




WHAT WE OFFER

 - Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

 - Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

 - Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

 - Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

 - Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún

 - Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role
We build AI-powered engines that make, localize, launch and learn from creative, using ElevenLabs’ full audio and video stack. Enterprise customers are already working with us. While our product teams focus on self-serve, these roles seed a dedicated enterprise engineering team: the people who make ElevenCreative work for our biggest customers and unblock enterprise deals. You sit between the customer and the product. You’ll talk to enterprise customers, understand their requirements, and decide whether to build a bespoke integration for them or a product improvement for everyone. Making that call well is the job.


Requirements

 - Has worked directly with customers as a forward-deployed engineer, solutions engineer or founding engineer at a B2B startup, including presenting to enterprise clients.

 - Strong full-stack product engineer, comfortable with integrations, APIs, auth and enterprise plumbing such as SSO, access control and security reviews.

 - Turns a customer’s ask into the real requirement: builds bespoke when it unblocks a deal, and generalizes when several customers want the same thing.

 - Ships end-to-end with little direction. There’s no PM to define everything first.

Bonus: experience with localization or TMS integrations, brand or marketing tooling, or adtech.

SECURITY ENGINEER, KUBERNETES

We protect the platform that runs X and SpaceXSI. We don’t just report issues, we actively look for real risks and exploits in our Kubernetes environments and turn them into durable fixes and tooling. You will secure the platform behind X and SpaceXSI’s infrastructure, products, and workloads. If you know pod and platform security, think in attack paths, and want to build the defenses that make the platform safer at scale, we want to hear from you.

We value a understanding of how Kubernetes can actually be abused – not just how it is configured. We prioritize shipping practical controls and tooling over writing policy documents, applying least privilege and defense-in-depth at fleet scale, delivering clear findings and fixes that platform teams can act on, and conducting safe, constrained validation that does not put production at risk.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Secure the platform end to end: nodes, clusters, pods, roles, tokens, secrets, service-to-service communication, and the supply chain
  • Find and remediate overprivileged permissions, dangerous pod and workload settings, and escalation paths in operators, admission, networking, identity, and monitoring
  • Assess our own platform the way an adversary would, including container and pod breakout, privilege escalation, and movement across workloads, using safe and constrained validation, then fix what you find
  • Design and build security tooling and automation, including AI-assisted analysis, that catches risky configuration and overprivilege before or after it ships
  • Strengthen identity and secrets handling so workloads receive only the access they need
  • Improve supply-chain security through secure base images, continuous scanning, and related controls
  • Review changes that affect RBAC, operators, ServiceAccounts, network policies, and anything running with elevated privileges
  • Partner with platform and product teams as a security owner, taking problems from identification through rollout
  • Contribute to fleet-wide hardening, policy enforcement, and safer defaults

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 3+ years in platform security, Kubernetes security, or offensive security against production infrastructure

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Deep knowledge of pod and workload security: privileged containers, capabilities, host namespaces, host path mounts, service accounts, RBAC, admission control, and network isolation
  • Working knowledge of identity, secrets, workload identity, service-to-service trust, supply chain, runtime, and cloud access
  • Able to think like an attacker, measure blast radius, and turn the path into a detection, control, or tool
  • Comfortable with operators, custom resources, Helm, and GitOps workflows
  • Able to build or modify security tooling in Go, Python, or Rust when a control needs automation
  • Bonus: Image scanning, SBOMs, secure base images, policy-as-co

jobs.title: Lead Data Scientist
jobs.description:
About Us

Firefly Neuroscience builds technology that helps improve how brain health careis delivered. Our technology focuses on making high-quality brain insights moreaccessible to clinicians and, ultimately, to the patients who depend on timely andaccurate care.

Make sure to read the full description below, and please apply immediately if you are confident you meet all the requirements.

By bringing greater objectivity and consistency to brain assessment, we helpreduce uncertainty in clinical decision-making and support more efficient pathsfrom evaluation to treatment. The goal is simple: clearer information, fewer delays,and better experiences for patients navigating complex care systems.

We are a growing team that values thoughtful problem-solving, high standards,and work that has real-world impact. If you are interested in contributing totechnology that meaningfully improves care while being built with care, Fireflyoffers the opportunity to do work that matters.

Role Summary

Firefly Neuroscience is hiring a Lead Data Scientist to own the neuroscience behind every number on our reports and to build what comes next. Our platform turns clinical EEG recordings into measures and reports that clinicians use in psychiatry and neurology practices. You will inherit that pipeline, verify it, and make it defensible; build and ship machine-learning models on real clinical data; and lay the groundwork for foundation models trained on neural data.

This is a hands-on, high-ownership role in a small, senior team. The science isyours end to end: you set the methodology, you ship in Python inside theengineering process, and you are the scientific authority our clinical advisors andcustomers rely on - with the Tech Lead, our clinical advisor, and companyleadership as direct partners. EEG expertise is not required - depth in neural orclinical data is. If your background is MRI or another modality, you will beexpected to come up to speed on EEG quickly.

Key Responsibilities
• Build, validate, deploy, and monitor machine-learning models on real clinicaldata - biomarker models, calibrated replacements for rules-based logic, andthe foundations for models trained at scale on our EEG corpus.
• Own the measures. For every number on a Firefly report, own what it is, how itis computed, what reference it is compared against, and its documentedlimitations.
• Verify and strengthen the existing analysis pipeline: reproduce and auditinherited methods, set acceptance criteria before comparisons, and fix whatdoes not hold up - with evidence that would stand up to clinical and regulatoryreview.
• Build and maintain the normative reference data our reports compare patientsagainst: reference population definition, covariate adjustment (age, sex), z-score construction, sample-size adequacy, and a process for refreshingnorms as data accumulates.
• Deliver sponsored-research analyses for external partners on time and to astandard that survives peer review, stating plainly what a sample can andcannot support.
• Partner with the Tech Lead on delivery and with our clinical advisor on clinicaldirection; ship through the engineering team's process, including changecontrol for any change to a measure or norm on the product.

Qualifications

Required
• 8+ years in a data science role.
• Master's degree or higher - or equivalent sustained hands-on research orindustry experience - in neuroscience, neuroimaging, clinical neurophysiology,biomedical engineering, or a closely related field, with enough depth to reasonindependently about what a brain measure reflects physiologically and whereit breaks down.
• Demonstrated experience building, shipping, and maintaining machine-learning or statistical models on neural or clinical data (EEG, MRI, or otherneuroimaging or physiological modalities), including sound handling of smallsamples, leakage, and class imbalance.
• Hands-on experience building and validating normative or reference datasets:defining reference populations

Most of what makes Together AI so valuable for customers is invisible from the outside. Optimizing kernels, scheduling, quantization, speculative decoding, and more create an industry-leading platform for inference and post-training at scale. This is a creator role. You are a technical storyteller. You'll produce social-native posts, technical blogs, performance benchmarks, demo and explainer videos, and thought leadership, all aimed at one outcome: building Together’s credibility with developers.   • Develop techniques to extract useful information from compliant tactile sensing in the presence of large sensor deformation, stretching or folding.
  • Diagnose and understand limitations of existing hardware or designs and inform future design requirements.
  • Evaluate novel sensing modalities to inform future hardware designs.

jobs.description:
About Decagon

Decagon is the leading conversational AI platform empowering every brand to deliver concierge customer experiences.

Our technology enables industry-defining enterprises like Avis Budget Group, Block’s Cash App and Square, Chime, Oura Health, and Hunter Douglas to deploy AI agents that power personalized, deeply satisfying interactions across voice, chat, email, SMS, and every other channel.

We’re building a future where customer experiences are being redefined from support tickets and hold music to faster resolutions, richer conversations, and deeper relationships. We’re proud to be backed by world-class investors who share that vision, including a16z, Accel, Bain Capital Ventures, Coatue, and Index Ventures, along with many others.

We’re an in-office company, driven by a shared commitment to excellence and velocity. Our values — Just Get It Done, Invent What Customers Want, Winner’s Mindset, and The Polymath Principle — shape how we work and grow as a team.



About the Team

Data Lifecycle at Decagon builds the systems that govern how sensitive customer data is handled throughout its lifetime: what we store, who can access it, how we redact it, and when we delete it. We turn complex privacy requirements into reliable infrastructure and product that customers can configure and trust.

This team is core to how Decagon scales. Our AI agents work with sensitive information across conversations, tool calls, and customer systems. The frameworks we build need to protect that data consistently across the platform, while preserving the context customers need to operate and improve their agents. A failure mode we debug in production becomes a guardrail, a test, or a piece of tooling that catches it everywhere.

Our systems run for companies like Hertz, American Airlines, and Notion across chat, voice, email, and SMS.



About the Role

You’ll design and build the platform infrastructure that let customers control how their data is collected, retained, redacted, and deleted. That means strong engineering underneath, and clear abstractions on top that hold up across different enterprise requirements without forking per customer.

You’ll work day to day with product management, governance, and security: understanding customer requirements, defining data handling guarantees, reviewing designs, and iterating through launch. You’ll stay close enough to customers to understand their privacy and operational needs in depth and to ensure what you’re building is actually right for them.

Engineers here own features end to end, from technical architecture through deployment and the iteration after it. On this team, that includes verifying that sensitive data is protected and the action actually completes. An understanding of durable and fault-tolerant systems is key.



In this role, you will

 - Build PII handling and redaction systems that identify and protect sensitive information across conversations, agent traces, and other customer data

 - Design configuration abstractions for redaction and retention policies that balance enterprise flexibility with clear, safe defaults

 - Build reliable data deletion workflows that propagate across storage systems and derived data, with retries, verification, and visibility into failures

 - Build self-serve tools and APIs that let customers configure, test, and understand their data lifecycle policies without relying on an engineer

 - Build LLM-backed systems that scan and detect data anomalies and violations

 - Train and/or tune models for detecting data of various forms (including PII and PHI)

 - Extend redaction and identification to multimodal agents, including images, attachments, voice notes, and documents.

 - Build monitoring and auditability that make it clear what data was processed, what remains, and where a policy has failed—without exposing sensitive information in the process

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Safety
jobs.description:

At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs.

In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic

In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.



About the role 

This is Bedrock's first dedicated Safety Technical Program Manager, a role built to establish the execution structure that lets us roll out new autonomy capabilities quickly without compromising safety rigor. As we scale to new machine types and expanded operational domains, we are evolving our safety practices toward more explicit, strategic execution.

You will own program execution for the safety, systems engineering, and state estimation work that makes autonomous heavy equipment safe to operate in the real world. This is a hands-on individual contributor role driving alignment and delivery across engineering, safety, autonomy, hardware, and field operations through influence, structure, and clear communication. You will be the connective tissue between safety strategy and technical delivery, making sure requirements are traceable, dependencies are visible, and risks surface early enough to act on. We are a startup that values agility. We believe that speed and safety are compatible when the traceability behind them is solid.



What you'll do

 - Own planning and strategic execution for the safety and systems portions of the autonomy roadmap, from requirements through validated field deployment.

 - Support safety requirements being traceable, reusable across platforms and sites, and integrated into roadmaps from inception, partnering with safety and systems engineering on hazard analysis, validation evidence, and release readiness.

 - Build and maintain the validation plan spanning simulation and on-site testing, ensuring system-level changes are verified before they reach customers.

 - Map and actively manage dependencies and tradeoffs across systems, hardware, software, state estimation, and safety, weighing safety impact alongside schedule impact and identifying single points of failure on the critical path before they slip.

 - Drive program reviews, risk, and change management for multi-disciplinary, safety-critical initiatives, and provide reporting on roadmap health, delivery status, and safety implications clear enough to support both executive decisions and customer-facing discussions.

 - Translate field signals into prioritized engineering work and tracking issues to resolution.



What you'll bring

 - 7+ years of technical program management experience, including 2+ years leading programs involving safety-critical or high-integrity systems.

 - Domain experience in robotics, autonomous systems, aerospace, or another physical-world safety-critical domain, with a working understanding of the software, firmware, and hardware stacks behind real-world autonomy.

 - Working familiarity with a functional safety standard, such as ISO 26

As Regional Director, you'll lead and scale this team across our most important public sector customers, own engagements from technical discovery through delivery, and build the partner track that extends this work through GSIs and consulting firms. BASIC QUALIFICATIONS

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE

jobs.title: Data Engineer, Marketing
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

About the role

The Data team at SpaceXSI is a small team that works across the company to inform business and product decisions, and we’re hiring the first member of our team to focus fully on marketing. Performance Marketing at SpaceXSI drives scaled acquisition across 10+ channels for Grok, Grok Bot, and our full portfolio of AI products, across consumer, SMB, startup, and enterprise audiences.

This role will sit in the central Data team and partner directly with Marketing leadership to own the measurement and analysis of performance marketing, growth marketing programs, and overall marketing measurement. You'll use your expertise to inform where the next dollar goes as we scale paid acquisition, while building the foundations of a world class marketing data team. Your job is to help us understand the impact of our activities and what we should do next.



What you'll do

 - Build and own the measurement layer for performance marketing: economics and performance by channel, campaign, audience, geo, and creative, across both PLG and Sales-Led revenue lines

 - Design incrementality tests (geo, audience, and conversion lift) with channel owners, and use the results to move budget and calibrate attribution, not just to fill a slide

 - Stand up and maintain our media-mix model, and pair it with test results to answer the big allocation questions: which channels to scale, which to cut, and where we're hitting saturation

 - Own the quality of the predictive LTV signal we send to Meta, Google, and the other networks: validate it against realized revenue, catch drift and breakage early, and partner with Data and Engineering to improve it

 - Keep pipeline source and campaign attribution separate and clean, so self-reported source, promo codes, click-based attribution, and CRM pipeline each answer their own question without double counting revenue



You may be a fit if

 - You have 7+ years of experience in marketing analytics, marketing science, or data science supporting paid acquisition

 - You have strong SQL and python skills and are comfortable building both data pipelines and predictive models

 - You've run hold-out or incrementality tests and worked with MMM and attribution models in production, and you know the limitations of each

 - You understand how ad platforms report, optimize, and ingest conversion signals, and you don't take platform-reported numbers at face value

 - You communicate clearly with channel managers, Finance, and leadership, and you're honest about what the data does and doesn't support

 - You're self-directed, comfortable owning ambiguous problems end to end
